findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow status is a free-form String, allowing any value including invalid combinations with other fields
findings.failure_mode: Any string (e.g. "sent", "deleted", "") can be assigned to status, enabling states like status="sent" with is_sent=false or is_validated=false, breaking invariants
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a domain enum `TelemetryStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` that encodes legal transitions

findings.problem: Lifecycle flag `is_validated` is a bare boolean separate from status, enabling contradictory states
findings.failure_mode: A telemetry item can have status="sent" and is_validated=false, or status="pending" and is_validated=true, both of which are logically contradictory and undetectable at compile time
findings.fix: Eliminate `is_validated` and `is_sent` booleans; encode lifecycle in the variant of a `TelemetryStatus` enum (e.g. `TelemetryStatus::Sent { validated: bool, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`)

findings.problem: Lifecycle flag `is_sent` is a bare boolean, creating the same illegal-state problem as `is_validated`
findings.failure_mode: Status and sent flags can diverge: status="pending" with is_sent=true is indistinguishable from a valid sent state by any invariant check
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent`; encode the sent state as an enum variant that owns lifecycle data

findings.problem: Optional lifecycle data stored as a separate `Option` field, independent of whether the item is actually in a sent state
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can hold Some value while status != "sent" and is_sent = false, leaking lifecycle data outside its proper state scope; or None while sent=true, losing required metadata
findings.fix: Move `sent_at_epoch_ms: u64` into a `TelemetryStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` variant so it is only present when the item is actually sent

findings.problem: Telemetry ID is a free-form `String` with no domain semantics, validation, or newtype protection
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, malformed IDs, and string-sized IDs all pass through without domain-level enforcement; callers cannot distinguish TelemetryWorkflow IDs from other string IDs at the type level
findings.fix: Introduce `struct TelemetryId(String)` or `struct TelemetryId([u8; N])` with a smart constructor that validates format, non-emptiness, and returns a typed error

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: TelemetryWorkflow) -> TelemetryWorkflow
findings.problem: parse boundary is not enforced: mark_sent accepts the raw struct and sets status via a raw string literal, allowing parse failures and invalid transitions to be silent
findings.failure_mode: Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly and mark_sent silently overwrites state without validating preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent)
findings.fix: Change signature to `fn mark_sent(item: TelemetryWorkflow) -> Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TelemetryError>` with a smart constructor that validates the item is in a valid pre-sent state before transitioning

findings.problem: String allocation via `.to_string()` in what should be pure core logic; string literal is also a magic string not tied to a domain enum
findings.failure_mode: Allocation failure in a hot path causes panic via `.to_string()` unwrapping internally; also entangles string allocation with domain state transitions
findings.fix: Replace `status` field with an enum; enum variant selection is zero-cost with no allocation

findings.construct: pub struct TelemetryWorkflow { ... } pub fn mark_sent ...
findings.problem: Domain model and state transition logic are fused together with no shell layer separation; no error taxonomy exists for transition failures
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state transitions silently succeed or are silently lost; callers cannot distinguish between "already sent", "not validated", and "unknown status" errors
findings.fix: Separate domain enum and pure transition function from shell; introduce `enum TelemetryError { AlreadySent, NotValidated }` and return `Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TelemetryError>`
